explanation: The NDC (January 1958) did not insist on a single rigid pattern; it left States to evolve patterns suited to local conditions, with the basic principles common.

notes.text: - **No PRIs:** **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram** (traditional/ADC bodies); Kerala, Assam, Tripura have PRIs.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
q: Which of the following committees was appointed by the Central Government to study the Community Development Programmes?
explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in 1957 to study the CDP and NES; Santhanam dealt with PR finances and elections, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao came later.

exam: APPSC Group-IV (Hostel Welfare Officers) 2012
q: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended
explanation: BRM's central recommendation was democratic decentralisation through elected bodies up to the district (Zila Parishad); blocks and village panchayats already existed and it reduced, not raised, the Collector's development role.

notes.text: - "Which State first implemented PR in 1959?" – **Rajasthan**; AP followed in 1959 itself ("both in 1959"). Not Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar, UP or Gujarat.

exam: APPSC Group-I 1999
q: The present pattern of Panchayat owes its parentage to
explanation: The present pattern of panchayats owes its parentage to the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957); Ashok Mehta's two-tier model was never adopted nationally.

notes.text: - AP books add that AP was the first to cover the **whole State at once**; Laxmikanth, NextGen and Rocket only say AP was **second**.

exam: APPSC Group-I 1990-91
q: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee Report is associated with
explanation:
Most keys: Panchayati Raj. Strictly: the committee was the study team on Community Projects and NES, so 'Community Development' is also linked (Laxmikanth ch.39 p.96).
The BRM report is identified with Panchayati Raj – its 'democratic decentralisation' became Panchayati Raj – although it was set up to review Community Development.

notes.text: - **Three-tier** PR first adopted by **Rajasthan**; by mid-1960s most States had PRIs.

explanation: BRM entrusted all planning and development to PRIs – decentralised planning as their basis; Mahalanobis and Gadgil (Planning) are not this, and Ashok Mehta came later.

notes.text: - **Three-tier** PR first adopted by **Rajasthan**; by mid-1960s most States had PRIs.

explanation: Decentralised planning through PRIs was recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, which entrusted all planning and development to them.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
q: Panchayat Raj is?
explanation: Panchayati Raj is seen as an inevitable extension of democracy to the grass roots – democratic decentralisation – not an evil, a mistaken ideology or obsolete.

notes.text: - "Which State first implemented PR in 1959?" – **Rajasthan**; AP followed in 1959 itself ("both in 1959"). Not Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar, UP or Gujarat.
- **Name "Panchayati Raj":** most keys credit **M.K. Gandhi** (Gram Swaraj; UPRO 2017); George Mathew credits **Nehru** with coining it – Nehru inaugurated it, BRM is its architect.

explanation: Rajasthan first adopted the three-tier system (Nagaur, 2 October 1959); Andhra Pradesh followed.

explanation: Panchayati Raj was first established on 2 October 1959 (Nagaur, Rajasthan).

explanation: The district is the key unit of administration (and, per G.V.K. Rao, 'the proper unit for planning and development'), above the mandal and revenue division.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
q: Which Committee recommended Constitutional status to the Panchayats?
explanation:
Most books and keys: L.M. Singhvi Committee. Strictly: Ashok Mehta (1978) and Thungon (1988) also recommended constitutional recognition (Laxmikanth ch.39 p.99, p.101).
The standard answer is the L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986), which asked for a new chapter in the Constitution; BRM did not ask for constitutional status.

notes.text: - **Finding:** PRIs had declined, yet they had **generated a new leadership** committed to development.
